method: per-kind probe (ls dist/types/<root>/, file counts, exported-symbol extraction), re-derivation of our crates' consumption against crates/ on disk
positive_control: cli (75 files + cli.d.ts + cli-commands.d.ts): the 39 CLI subcommands enumerated in §00 §3.2 are THIS surface. Every one was counted, classified, and mapped. If cli is not fully covered, the census is broken.
anti_vacuity: 8 roots enumerated with file counts and export symbols; zero-surface enumeration impossible

rows.omp_alternative: KagiSearchData/KagiSearchOptions/KagiErrorResponse — OMP's built-in web search (Kagi + Perplexity). The orchestrator does not search the web; it orchestrates panes
rows.refusal: no crate's job is web search; the agent inside each pane has its own web access

rows.omp_alternative: ExaSearchResponse/MCPToolWrapperConfig — MCP-wrapped Exa search; same refusal as web
STTController/EndpointerConfig/DownloadProgress — speech-to-text for voice input; no crate consumes speech
StreamingAudioPlayer/SpeechEnhancer/SpeakableStream — text-to-speech output; no crate produces audio

RemoteDirEntry/RemoteFileReadOptions/RemotePathKind — OMP's SSH file-transfer types. Our rch dependency owns SSH transport (rchd daemon + SSH prober); subprocess-contract owns process-group/drain semantics. The VALIDATE disposition means: we depend on SSH being available without consuming OMP's SSH types, tested by rch workers probe (proven live: ✓ OK 40ms)

InternalUrl extends URL, AgentProtocolHandler, ArtifactProtocolHandler, HistoryProtocolHandler — the scheme resolver for omp://, artifact://, memory://, skill://, agent://. Every pane session uses these URLs; we parse them informally in strings. Test: pin the scheme grammar as a golden fixture when M1 lands (omp-orchestrator compiles against omp-types)

The 29 built-in tools (AskTool, BashToolCallEvent, EditToolCallEvent, GlobToolCallEvent, GrepToolCallEvent, ReadToolCallEvent, etc.) plus 3 hidden. These are the AGENT's tool surface inside each pane — the agent uses them, not the orchestrator. The orchestrator dispatches WORK to panes; what the agent does inside the pane is S6 (§11.1: 'the agent's own business; we observe only')
rows.refusal: no crate's job is to consume the agent's internal tool calls; observing them is tick-monitor's job via pane capture

rows.omp_alternative: ResolvedCliArgv + 39 CLI subcommands (acp, agents, auth-broker, bench, browser-relay, cleanse, commit, completions, compress, config, dry-balance, gallery, gc...). We consume omp --mode=rpc (omp-rpc-session lib.rs:99) and probe omp --help (omp-inventory-map census). The CLI surface IS the one we wrap most directly
